newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST - Japan July industrial production seen up.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Japan July industrial production seen up.

text.p: Japan's industrial production for July is likely to show growth after a sharp fall in June, but sluggish semiconductor output will continue to cast a dark shadow over future prospects, economists said on Tuesday.
Economists polled by Reuters forecast on average that July industrial production will show 3.4 percent growth from the month before and 4.5 percent from a year earlier.
The forecasts ranged from growth of 2.8 percent to 4.0 percent month-on-month and 3.9 to 5.1 percent year-on-year.
In June, industrial output fell 4.3 percent from the previous month and 1.0 percent from a year earlier.

The expected month-on-month rise in July was mainly due to more working days that month than in June. Without that as a factor, the July output figures would have likely posted a fall due to declining semiconductor production, said Soichi Okuda, a senior economist at Nippon Credit Bank.
Year-on-year growth was due to an increase in automobile production ahead of the launch of new models this autumn, economists said.
"You can say that the output is still on a gradual upward trend, but in reality, I think it's more like crawling sideways," Okuda said.

The data, to be announced on Friday at 0630 GMT, "would not be of the sort that would prompt the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to change its monetary policy immediately," said Shuji Shirota, an economist at Yamaichi Research Institute. Industry sources say the BOJ has been watching production figures, considered a key indicator for assessing the state of the economy.

Overall inventory levels are likely to remain high, as a buildup of stocks in the semiconductor industry due to the worsening supply/demand situation will offset the positive effects from the paper, pulp and steel industries finishing their inventory adjustments, economists said.
Looking ahead, economists see August output dropping sharply due to summer holidays, but say the figure should rise again in September as many carmakers launch new models.

On the demand side, private consumption may pick up towards the end of this year as consumers buy durable goods and houses ahead of an increase in the consumption tax to five percent next April from the current three percent.

But this may not lead to improved domestic output as consumers increasingly turn to cheaper imported goods. Demand for home electronics items such as TVs and refrigerators may also slow in the coming months, economists said.
Economists said they want to see whether an increase in automobile production will help offset a drop in semiconductor output. The following are forecasts for July industrial production data:
